title: The morning the sea walked out of Lisbon 🌊
subject: tsunami
description:
Would you have run toward the water or away? 👇

On All Saints' Day, November 1, 1755, an earthquake, a tsunami and a firestorm destroyed most of Lisbon. The same tsunami crossed the Atlantic to Barbados, and the disaster changed how Europe thought about earthquakes.

Sources: Wikipedia ("1755 Lisbon earthquake"), Britannica ("Lisbon earthquake of 1755"), Europeana ("What was the impact of the Great Lisbon Earthquake in 1755?")

scenes.text: The water drained out of Lisbon's harbor.
It was 9:40 a.m. on All Saints' Day, November 1, 1755. An earthquake had just shaken the city.
Survivors ran to the docks and watched a plain of mud appear, littered with shipwrecks.
About 40 minutes after the quake, the sea rushed back up the Tagus.
Candles lit for the holiday had already set off a firestorm across the city.
85% of Lisbon's buildings were destroyed. The same tsunami crossed the Atlantic to Barbados.
